title: The new covenant (Hebrews 8)
hook: Hebrews quotes Jeremiah: I will write my laws on their hearts
tomorrow: if you can pray anywhere, why does Hebrews care who shows up?

segments.voice: Melchizedek, the king from Salem with no beginning and no end in the story, and a priest who never hands off. He always lives to pray. Now Hebrews turns from the priest to the promise.
screen: `HE ALWAYS LIVES TO PRAY.` → `FROM THE PRIEST TO THE PROMISE.`

segments.voice: Nobody needs a tutorial for their best friend's laugh, or the words to a song they grew up on. Some things you know so well you can't remember learning them. Keep that in mind, because Hebrews has an odd moment. It's a long, careful lesson, argument after argument. And in the middle of it, the writer quotes a promise that sounds like it would put every teacher out of work: "And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest." Why would a teaching letter quote that?
screen: `KNOWN BY HEART.` → `A LESSON QUOTING NO MORE LESSONS.` → `WHY QUOTE THAT?`

segments.voice: The promise comes from the prophet Jeremiah, and Hebrews quotes it at length. It opens: "Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah." A covenant is a binding promise between two parties. Then the clue to the puzzle, where this one is kept: "I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people." There's the answer. The knowing promised here isn't a set of facts you could look up. It's the way you know a voice, or a person. Teaching doesn't vanish. It moves inside, until knowing and wanting start to line up. And under it all, mercy: "their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more." Two readings meet here, and this lesson ranks neither. Jeremiah spoke these words to the house of Israel and the house of Judah, and Jewish readers read them within Israel's own covenant. The writer of Hebrews reads them through Jesus, the high priest of the chapters before. The detail to tell a friend tonight: the same promise lives in two Bibles, in Jeremiah's own pages and again, quoted, in Hebrews.
screen: `A NEW COVENANT, FROM JEREMIAH.` · `WRITTEN IN THEIR HEARTS.` · `KNOWING A PERSON, NOT FACTS.` · `TWO READINGS, NONE RANKED.` · then, large: `ON THEIR HEARTS.`

segments.voice: Say one short line you know by heart, out loud and slowly: a verse, a grace before meals, something a grandparent always said. Notice that you didn't need a page to find it. Then say it once more, softer, and let the quiet after it be the rest of the sit.
The new covenant. A promise from Jeremiah, quoted in Hebrews eight: laws put into the mind and written on the heart.
Keep this one: on their hearts, not on stone and not on a screen. Until tomorrow.

fork.setup: your little cousin memorized a verse to win a sticker at church, then forgot it a week later. your aunt sighs: what's the point? what does Hebrews 8's promise point toward?
options: stop memorizing; the heart doesn't need words.

fork.reveal: I will write them in their hearts: the promise is knowing God the way you know a person, which words learned by heart can help, not replace.

original.note: Greek: covenant; the word in Hebrews 8 for the covenant Jeremiah promised.

trapdoor: what you thought: the new covenant means God threw out the old one.
what it means: Jeremiah's promise of laws written on hearts, read by Hebrews through Jesus and by Jewish readers within Israel's covenant.
what a scholar hears: the King James words differ between the two books: Jeremiah has I will put my law in their inward parts, and Hebrews has my laws into their mind.

chat.says: surgery went ok!! pop can't hold his bible yet but he said a whole psalm to the night nurse. how??
options: It's written on his heart, like the promise Hebrews 8 quotes. What's learned by heart stays with you.
He doesn't need it now. Hebrews 8 says the new covenant replaces the written Bible altogether.
It's just memory tricks. Hebrews 8 says God's laws belong on stone, not inside people.
chat.meaning: Hebrews 8 quotes Jeremiah: I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts. Pop carries what he's learned.
